description: Committee recommends $121,750 bonus payment to SREDA.
Committee recommends SREDA's 2026 performance indicators.
SREDA launching Concierge program in May for businesses.
Program supports expanding and new businesses in key sectors.

chips.text: Taxpayers fund a recommended $121,750 bonus payment to SREDA.
SREDA will launch its Concierge program at the May 12th State of the Economy Summit.

description: Committee recommends approving 2026 tax abatements for six businesses.
These businesses represent $25.7 million investment and 90 new jobs.
Four additional projects will add $142 million investment and 200 jobs.

chips.text: SREDA highlighted incentives attract new businesses and create jobs.

description: Committee recommends $3,794,000 loan for future city operations land.
Funds 3815 Wanuskewin Road and 3802 Arthur Rose Avenue.
Loan repaid from lease payments at 3.75% internal rate.
Recommends buying 4 acres for a new French school in Kensington.
Costs $3.57 million from the Elementary School Land Levy Reserve.
City will lease land for 400 students and 90 childcare spaces.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer suggested French schools might fit high school land levies.
City now owns school land, leasing it to school divisions.
Will the elementary school levy be sufficient for future Kensington schools?
Province committed to long-term planning and school land cost-sharing.

description: City to negotiate tenant licenses for Gather Local Market.
Also for Ideas Inc. at 120 Sonnenschein Way.
Agreements will be at or near market rates.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois noted the city has lost significant money on these properties.
Community benefit criteria in future RFP may lead to subsidized rental rates.
City will issue an RFP for an overall operator for both buildings.

description: Recommend increasing capital project budgets by $11.5 million from grants.
Funding supports waste reduction, park upgrades, and energy efficiency.
Includes $9.7 million for water and sewer capacity improvements.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned funding for $24.7M water and sewer project.
Funding includes $150,000 for waste reduction and $450,000 for energy efficiency.

description: Increases City Manager's lease approval limit to $40,000.
Repeals several old, repaid borrowing bylaws.
Reallocates $580,000 federal Natural Infrastructure Fund money.
Adjusts funding for nine capital projects.
Ensures full utilization of federal grant funding.

chips.text: Funds support creating, expanding, restoring natural and hybrid infrastructure.

description: Committee recommends 5-year tax exemption for two soccer centres.
Kinsmen/Henk Ruys and Saskatoon Soccer Centres would receive exemption.
The exemption would begin in 2026 and end in 2030.

chips.text: Saskatoon Soccer Inc., a non-profit, would receive the tax exemption.

description: Renew seven farmland leases on 4,500 acres of city land.
Leases average $53 per acre, ranging $35 to $70.
Leases average 470 acres, ranging 359 to 622 acres.

chips.text: Farmers holding city-owned agricultural land leases.
Lease renewals now require committee approval due to increased value.

description: Transfers land sale proceeds to South Caswell Hill development.
Funds demolition of 301 24th Street West transit buildings.

chips.text: Affects future redevelopment in South Caswell Hill neighborhood.

description: Committee recommends Council acknowledge two reports.
City investments generated $27.9 million revenue in 2025.
TD Asset Management began managing the city's growth portfolio.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer expressed concern about significant, unpredictable investment variances.
Administration directed to provide an updated investment variance forecast at fall budget.

description: Board of Revision handled 1,500 property assessment appeals.
Adjusted $452 million in property values in 2025.

chips.text: Councilor Donauer questioned why Board of Revision reports are not prioritized on the agenda.
Saskatoon property owners are affected by assessment appeal decisions.
